user_error_text: My PC does not turn on at all when I press the power button
symptoms: No power, no lights, no fan movement, completely dead
cause: Power supply issue, loose power cable, faulty power button, or motherboard problem
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check Power Source (VERY IMPORTANT)
Make sure the power cable is firmly plugged into the PC and wall socket
Try a different wall socket
If using a power strip / UPS, bypass it and connect directly to the wall
Look for any loose or damaged power cable
📌 If there is no power reaching the PC, it will not turn on at all.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Verify Power Supply (PSU) Switch
Check the switch at the back of the PSU
It must be set to ON ( | ), not OFF ( O )
If your PSU has a voltage selector, ensure it matches your region (usually 230V)
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Look for Any Signs of Power
Do you see any lights on the motherboard or case?
Do fans spin for even a second?
Do you hear any click or sound?
✔️ No lights / sounds → likely power supply or cable issue
✔️ Lights but no start → possible motherboard or power button issue
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Check the Power Button Connection
Turn off power and unplug the PC
Open the case
Locate the front panel connectors on the motherboard
Ensure the POWER SW cable is properly connected
🔎 Test tip:
Briefly touch the power switch pins with a screwdriver
If PC turns on → Power button is faulty
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Reseat Main Power Cables
Remove and reconnect:
24-pin motherboard power cable
8-pin CPU power cable
Make sure they click firmly into place
Loose cables can prevent startup completely.
verification: PC should turn on and display POST screen or boot into Windows
tag: power, hardware, startup

user_error_text: My computer gets stuck on the restarting screen and never loads Windows
symptoms: Windows restart screen loops indefinitely, never completes boot
cause: Corrupted boot files, problematic Windows update, driver conflict, or USB device blocking boot
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Force Restart (Quick Fix)
Hold the Power button for 10 seconds to shut down the PC
Wait 30 seconds
Turn the PC back ON
📌 Sometimes Windows gets stuck due to a temporary process hang.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disconnect External Devices
Power OFF the computer
Unplug USB devices (pen drive, printer, external HDD, webcam, etc.)
Keep only keyboard + mouse
Turn the PC ON again
✔️ Faulty USB devices can block Windows during restart.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Enter Automatic Repair Mode
If it still loops:
Turn ON the PC
When Windows logo appears → force shutdown
Repeat 2–3 times
Windows should show "Preparing Automatic Repair"
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Run Startup Repair
In Automatic Repair:
Click Advanced options
Go to Troubleshoot → Advanced options
Select Startup Repair
Choose your Windows account
✔️ This fixes boot files automatically.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Boot into Safe Mode
If Startup Repair fails:
Advanced options → Startup Settings
Click Restart
Press 4 or F4 → Safe Mode
If Safe Mode loads:
Press Win + R, type msconfig
Go to Services
✔️ Check Hide all Microsoft services
Click Disable all
Restart normally
📌 This removes problematic drivers or software.
verification: Windows should boot normally after completing these steps
tag: boot, restart, loop, windows

user_error_text: My device is connected to Wi-Fi, but the internet is not working.
symptoms: Wi-Fi shows connected but websites do not load, no internet access
cause: Router/modem issue, incorrect IP configuration, proxy settings, or ISP problem
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check If Internet Works on Other Devices
Test Wi-Fi on another phone or laptop
If no devices have internet → router or ISP issue
If other devices work → problem is with your PC
📌 This step helps isolate the problem quickly.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart Network Devices (VERY IMPORTANT)

Turn OFF:
Modem
Router
Your computer
Wait 2 minutes
Turn ON in this order:
Modem → wait for stable lights
Router → wait 1 minute
Computer
✔️ Fixes most temporary network and IP issues.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Forget & Reconnect Wi-Fi
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Wi-Fi
Click Manage known networks
Select your Wi-Fi → Forget
Reconnect and enter the password again
📌 Fixes wrong or corrupted network profiles.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Check IP Address Configuration
Press Win + R → type cmd → Enter
Type:
ipconfig
🔎 Look at IPv4 Address:
If it starts with 169.254.x.x → No valid IP received
✔️ Fix:
ipconfig /release
ipconfig /renew
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Disable Proxy & VPN
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Proxy
Turn OFF "Use a proxy server"
Disconnect any VPN software
Restart the PC
📌 Proxy/VPN misconfiguration is a common cause.
verification: Internet should work after reconnecting and fixing IP configuration
tag: network, wifi, internet, connection

user_error_text: There is no sound coming from my computer
symptoms: No audio output from speakers or headphones, system sounds do not play
cause: Muted volume, wrong output device, audio driver issue, or disabled audio services
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check Basic Sound Settings (VERY IMPORTANT)
Click the speaker icon in the bottom-right corner
Make sure: ❌ Not muted / 🔊 Volume is above 50%
Play a YouTube video or Windows test sound
📌 Many no-sound issues are simply mute or low volume.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Select the Correct Audio Output Device
Right-click speaker icon → Sound settings
Under Output, choose the correct device: [Speakers (Realtek / Internal) / Headphones / HDMI / Monitor audio / Bluetooth device]
Click Test
✔️ Wrong output device = no sound even when volume is high.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Restart Audio Services
Press Win + R
Type services.msc → Enter
Restart: Windows Audio / Windows Audio Endpoint Builder
📌 Fixes stuck or crashed audio services.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Check & Fix Audio Driver (MOST COMMON CAUSE)
Press Win + X → Device Manager
Expand Sound, video and game controllers
If you see: ⚠️ Yellow warning → driver issue
Right-click your audio device: Update driver
Restart PC (Windows reinstalls driver)
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Enable Speakers in Playback Devices
Right-click speaker icon → Sounds
Go to Playback tab
Right-click inside → ✔️ Show Disabled Devices
Enable Speakers
Set it as Default Device
📌 Disabled speakers = silence.
verification: Sound should play when testing audio output
tag: audio, sound, driver, speakers

user_error_text: My USB device is not recognized by the computer
symptoms: USB device not detected, no notification when plugged in, device manager shows unknown device
cause: Faulty USB device, damaged USB port, power saving settings, or USB controller driver issue
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check the USB Device Itself (VERY IMPORTANT)
Unplug the USB device and plug it back in firmly
Try the device on another computer
❌ Not detected there → USB device is faulty
✔️ Works there → problem is with your PC
Inspect the USB connector for damage or dirt
📌 This immediately tells you whether it's a device or PC issue.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart the Computer
Restart Windows normally
Plug in the USB device after Windows fully loads
✔️ Fixes temporary USB controller glitches.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Try Different USB Ports
Try all USB ports on the PC
On desktops, prefer rear motherboard ports
Avoid USB hubs or extension cables
📌 A damaged or underpowered port can cause this error.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Disable USB Power Saving (MOST EFFECTIVE)
Press Win + X → Device Manager
Expand Universal Serial Bus controllers
For each USB Root Hub: Right-click → Properties → Power Management tab
❌ Uncheck Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power
Click OK and restart
✔️ Prevents Windows from shutting down USB ports.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Reinstall USB Controllers
In Device Manager
Expand Universal Serial Bus controllers
Right-click and Uninstall:
USB Root Hub / USB Host Controller / Unknown USB Device (if shown)
Restart the PC
📌 Windows will automatically reinstall fresh USB drivers.
verification: USB device should be recognized and appear in File Explorer or Device Manager
tag: usb, driver, device, hardware

user_error_text: I forgot my Windows login password and cannot access my PC
symptoms: Cannot log into Windows account, password prompt appears but password is forgotten
cause: Forgotten password, account lockout, or password reset needed
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Reset Password (Microsoft Account) — BEST & EASIEST
✔️ Use this if you sign in with an email address (Outlook / Hotmail / Live)
Steps:
On another device (phone or PC), open a browser
Go to: account.microsoft.com/password
Reset your password using:
Email
Phone number
Security code
Restart your PC
Log in using the new password
📌 Your PC must be connected to the internet.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Use PIN / Picture Password (If Set Before)
On the login screen, click Sign-in options
Try:
PIN
Picture password
✔️ Many users forget the password but still have a working PIN.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Reset Local Account Password (Advanced)
Use this if your account is NOT a Microsoft account.
Steps:
Restart PC
Interrupt boot 2–3 times (power off during Windows logo)
You'll see Preparing Automatic Repair
Go to:
Advanced options → Troubleshoot → Advanced options
Startup Repair (try first)
If Startup Repair fails, continue.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Reset Windows While Keeping Files (SAFE)
✔️ This is the most reliable local account fix.
Steps:
Automatic Repair screen → Troubleshoot
Click Reset this PC
Choose Keep my files
Select Local reinstall
Follow on-screen steps
📌 This removes the password but keeps:
Documents
Pictures
Videos
❌ Apps will be removed.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Use Another Admin Account (If Exists)
On the login screen, switch users
Log in with another Administrator account
Open:
Control Panel → User Accounts
Reset password for your account
verification: Should be able to log in with new password or PIN
tag: password, login, security, account

user_error_text: My laptop overheats and shuts down automatically
symptoms: Laptop gets very hot, fan runs loudly, system shuts down unexpectedly, performance throttles
cause: Dust buildup, poor airflow, failing cooling fan, dried thermal paste, or high CPU/GPU load
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Improve Airflow (VERY IMPORTANT)
Place the laptop on a hard, flat surface
❌ Avoid beds, pillows, or laps (they block vents)
Keep air vents fully clear
Use the laptop in a cool room
📌 Poor airflow is the #1 cause of overheating.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Clean Dust From Vents & Fan
Power OFF and unplug the laptop
Use compressed air to blow dust out of vents
If experienced, open the back cover and:
Clean cooling fan
Clean heatsink
✔️ Dust blocks airflow and traps heat.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Check If the Cooling Fan Is Working
Turn on the laptop and listen:
✔️ Fan noise = OK
❌ No sound = fan may be dead
Use tools like HWMonitor or Core Temp to check temperatures
⚠️ CPU temps above 90°C = overheating.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Reduce CPU & GPU Load
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc → Task Manager
End unnecessary apps
Disable heavy startup programs
Avoid gaming or rendering until fixed
📌 High CPU usage = more heat.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Replace Thermal Paste (Advanced but Effective)
Thermal paste dries after 2–3 years
Replacing it can reduce temps by 10–20°C
Requires laptop disassembly (do only if experienced)
✔️ Very effective for older laptops.
verification: Laptop should run cooler and not shut down unexpectedly
tag: overheating, thermal, hardware, fan

user_error_text: I am getting a blue screen error on Windows 10/11.
symptoms: Blue screen appears, system crashes, STOP code displayed, automatic restart
cause: Driver conflict, hardware failure, memory issues, corrupted system files, or incompatible software
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Note the STOP CODE (VERY IMPORTANT)
On the blue screen, look for text like:
CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED / IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL / MEMORY_MANAGEMENT / SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
📌 Write this down — it tells us the exact cause.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart in Safe Mode
1.Restart the PC
2.If BSOD repeats, force shutdown 2–3 times
3.When Automatic Repair appears:
	Advanced options → Troubleshoot
	Advanced options → Startup Settings
	Restart → Press 4 (Safe Mode)
✔️ Safe Mode loads only essential drivers.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Remove Recent Changes

If BSOD started recently:
	Uninstall new software
	Unplug new hardware
	Roll back recent drivers
	Uninstall recent Windows updates (Settings → Windows Update → Update history)
📌 Most BSODs are caused by recent changes.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Update or Reinstall Drivers
1.Press Win + X → Device Manager
2.Check for ⚠️ yellow warning icons
3.Update these drivers first:
	Display / Graphics
	Network
	Storage (SATA / NVMe)
4.If issue started after driver update → Roll back driver
✔️ Bad drivers = #1 BSOD cause.
verification: System should boot normally without blue screen errors
tag: bsod, blue screen, crash, driver

user_error_text: My laptop turns on, but the screen stays black
symptoms: Laptop powers on but display remains black, no image on screen, backlight may be off
cause: Brightness settings, display toggle, hardware failure, loose connections, or RAM issues
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check Brightness & Display Toggle (VERY IMPORTANT)
	Press Fn + Brightness Up key (usually F5 / F6 / F7 / F8)
	Press Fn + Display Switch key (often Fn + F4 / F5 / F8)
📌 Sometimes the screen is on but brightness is set to zero or display is switched off.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Hard Reset the Laptop
1.Power OFF the laptop
2.Unplug the charger
3.Remove the battery (if removable)
4.Hold Power button for 30 seconds
5.Reconnect charger and turn ON
✔️ Clears static power and fixes many black-screen issues.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Test With an External Monitor
Connect laptop to a TV or external monitor (HDMI / VGA)
Turn laptop ON
Press Fn + Display Switch key
Result:
✔️ External display works → laptop screen or cable issue
❌ No display anywhere → GPU / motherboard issue
📌 This is a key diagnostic step.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Look for Signs of Life
Check carefully:
	Caps Lock light toggles ON/OFF?
	Do you hear Windows startup sound?
	Fan spinning normally?
✔️ Yes → display problem
❌ No → system not booting properly
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Reseat RAM (Advanced but Effective)

⚠️ Do this only if you're comfortable opening the laptop.
	Power OFF and unplug
	Remove back cover
	Remove RAM stick
	Clean contacts gently
	Reinsert RAM firmly
	Power ON
📌 Loose RAM commonly causes black screen on startup.
verification: Screen should display normally after fixing the issue
tag: black screen, display, laptop, startup

user_error_text: Windows is not booting after installing the latest update
symptoms: Windows fails to boot after update installation, stuck on loading screen, automatic repair loop
cause: Corrupted update files, incompatible update, driver conflict, or boot file corruption
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Wait on "Undoing Changes" Screen (VERY IMPORTANT)
	If you see "Undoing changes made to your computer"
	Wait 20–40 minutes
	Do NOT force shutdown too quickly
📌 Windows may still be rolling back the update.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Force Automatic Repair Mode
If Windows never loads:
1.Power ON the PC
2.When Windows logo appears → hold Power button to shut down
3.Repeat 2–3 times
4.You should see Preparing Automatic Repair
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Run Startup Repair
From Automatic Repair:
	Advanced options → Troubleshoot
	Advanced options → Startup Repair
	Select your account and continue
✔️ Fixes broken boot files caused by updates.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Uninstall the Latest Windows Update (MOST EFFECTIVE)
If Startup Repair fails:
1.Advanced options → Troubleshoot
2.Uninstall Updates
3.Choose one:
	✅ Uninstall latest quality update (recommended first)
	If still fails → Uninstall latest feature update

📌 This directly removes the update that broke Windows.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Boot Into Safe Mode
1.Advanced options → Startup Settings
2.Click Restart
3.Press 4 or F4 → Safe Mode

If Safe Mode works:
	Uninstall recently installed drivers
	Disable startup apps
	Restart normally

✔️ Confirms Windows itself is still functional.
verification: Windows should boot normally after uninstalling the problematic update
tag: boot, update, windows, startup

user_error_text: My PC is stuck in an automatic repair loop
symptoms: PC continuously loops in automatic repair, cannot boot into Windows, repair fails repeatedly
cause: Corrupted boot files, external device blocking boot, broken Windows update, or driver conflict
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Power Cycle & Remove External Devices (VERY IMPORTANT)
Turn OFF the PC completely
Unplug all USB devices (pen drives, printers, external HDDs)
For laptops: unplug charger and remove battery (if possible)
Hold Power button for 30 seconds
Reconnect power and turn ON

📌 External devices can block boot and cause repair loops.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Enter Advanced Startup Options
When Automatic Repair appears:
	Click Advanced options
	Select Troubleshoot

If you cannot reach this screen, force shutdown 2–3 times during startup.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Run Startup Repair (Once Only)
	Troubleshoot → Advanced options → Startup Repair
	Select your Windows account

⚠️ If Startup Repair fails once, do not repeat multiple times — move to next step.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Uninstall Recent Windows Updates (MOST EFFECTIVE)

Troubleshoot → Advanced options → Uninstall Updates
Choose:
	Uninstall latest quality update
	If still looping → Uninstall latest feature update

✔️ Broken updates are the #1 cause of repair loops.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Boot into Safe Mode

Troubleshoot → Advanced options → Startup Settings
Click Restart
Press 4 (Safe Mode)

If Safe Mode loads:
	Uninstall recently installed drivers/software
	Disable startup programs
	Restart normally

📌 Confirms Windows core files still work.
verification: PC should boot normally without entering repair loop
tag: repair loop, boot, automatic repair, windows

user_error_text: My computer freezes randomly while I am using it
symptoms: System freezes randomly, becomes unresponsive, mouse/keyboard stop working, requires hard restart
cause: Overheating, high CPU/RAM usage, driver issues, faulty RAM, or hardware failure
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check for Overheating (VERY IMPORTANT)
1.Touch the laptop bottom / desktop case: Very hot? → overheating
2.Install HWMonitor or Core Temp
3.Check temperatures: CPU > 85–90°C = problem

✔️ Fix:
Clean dust from fans
Ensure vents are not blocked
Use laptop on hard surface
Replace thermal paste (older systems)

📌 Overheating is the #1 cause of random freezes.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Check CPU & RAM Usage
1.Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc → Task Manager
2.Watch:CPU usage / Memory usage / Disk usage

❌ If CPU or Disk stays at 100% → freeze cause found
✔️ End unnecessary apps
✔️ Disable heavy startup programs
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Update or Roll Back Drivers
1.Press Win + X → Device Manager
2.Update these first: Graphics (GPU) / Storage (SATA / NVMe) / Network
3.If freezing started after update → Roll back driver

📌 Bad drivers commonly cause system hangs.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Test RAM (Memory Errors)

1.Press Win + R
2.Type mdsched.exe
3.Restart and test

❌ Errors found → faulty RAM stick (replace it)
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Event Viewer (Advanced)
1.Press Win + X → Event Viewer
2.Go to: Windows Logs → System
3.Look for Critical / Error events during freeze time

📌 Helps identify failing drivers or hardware.
verification: System should run smoothly without random freezes
tag: freeze, hang, performance, overheating

user_error_text: My computer has suddenly become very slow Windows 10 / 11
symptoms: Sudden performance degradation, slow response times, laggy interface, applications take long to load
cause: Background processes, high resource usage, malware, too many startup programs, or temporary file buildup
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Restart & Check for Temporary Issues (VERY IMPORTANT)
Restart your computer once
After reboot, wait 5 minutes (Windows may be finishing background tasks)
Test performance again
📌 This fixes many short-term slowdowns.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Check Task Manager for High Usage
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc → Task Manager
Check: [CPU | Memory | (RAM)Disk]
🔎 Common problems:
Disk stuck at 100%
Memory above 80–90%
One app using too much CPU

✔️ End unnecessary tasks
✔️ Note the app causing high usage
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Disable Unnecessary Startup Programs
Task Manager → Startup tab
Disable apps you don't need at startup: [Launchers | Auto updaters | Chat apps]
📌 This significantly improves boot and overall speed.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Scan for Malware & Viruses
Open Windows Security
Run a Full Scan
Remove detected threats
📌 Malware can cause sudden performance drops.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Clean Temporary Files
Press Win + R → type temp → delete files
Again Win + R → type %temp% → delete
Use Disk Cleanup on C: drive
✔️ Frees space and improves responsiveness.
verification: Computer should respond faster and run more smoothly
tag: slow, performance, lag, slowdown

user_error_text: Disk usage stays at 100% all the time on Windows 10/11
symptoms: Disk usage constantly at 100%, system becomes slow, applications freeze, high disk activity
cause: SysMain (Superfetch), Windows Search indexing, virtual memory issues, malware, or disk defragmentation
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Identify the Cause in Task Manager (VERY IMPORTANT)
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc → Task Manager
Click the Disk column to sort
🔎 Common culprits: [System SysMain | (Superfetch) | Windows | Update Antivirus | Disk defragmenter]
📌 This helps decide the correct fix.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disable SysMain (Superfetch) — MOST EFFECTIVE
Press Win + R
Type services.msc
Find SysMain
Right-click → Stop
Right-click → Properties
Set Startup type → Disabled
Restart PC
✔️ Dramatically reduces disk usage on HDD systems.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Stop Windows Search (Indexing)
In services.msc
Find Windows Search
Stop the service
Set Startup type → Disabled
📌 Indexing can overload slow disks.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Reset Virtual Memory (Pagefile)
Control Panel → System → Advanced system settings
Performance → Settings
Advanced → Virtual memory
Set to System managed size
Restart PC
📌 Wrong pagefile settings cause disk thrashing.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Scan for Malware
Open Windows Security
Run Full scan
Remove threats
✔️ Malware can keep disk busy constantly.
verification: Disk usage should drop to normal levels (under 50%)
tag: disk usage, 100 percent, performance, sysmain

user_error_text: Windows Update keeps failing with an error message
symptoms: Windows Update fails repeatedly, error codes displayed, updates cannot be installed
cause: Corrupted update cache, insufficient disk space, network issues, service problems, or driver conflicts
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Note the Error Code (VERY IMPORTANT)
Look for codes like: [0x80070020 | 0x800f0831 | 0x8024401c | 0x80073712]
📌 Error codes help identify whether the issue is files, drivers, services, or internet-related.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart PC & Check Internet
Restart your computer once
Make sure internet is stable (no VPN / proxy)
Avoid mobile hotspot if possible
✔️ Many update failures are temporary.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Run Windows Update Troubleshooter
Go to Settings → System → Troubleshoot
Click Other troubleshooters
Run Windows Update
Apply suggested fixes
📌 Automatically fixes common update problems.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Stop Update Services & Clear Cache (MOST EFFECTIVE)
Press Win + R → type services.msc
Stop these services: Windows Update & Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS)
Open File Explorer and go to: C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution
Delete all files and folders inside
Restart the services
Restart your PC
✔️ Fixes corrupted update downloads.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Free Disk Space
Ensure at least 20–25 GB free on C: drive
Run Disk Cleanup
Delete temporary files
✔️ Low disk space causes update failures.
verification: Windows Update should install successfully
tag: windows update, update failure, error code

user_error_text: My PC is stuck on the loading screen and does not start
symptoms: PC stuck on Windows loading screen, spinning dots or logo, never reaches login screen
cause: Corrupted boot files, external device blocking boot, broken Windows update, or driver conflict
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Wait & Restart Properly (VERY IMPORTANT)
If it's the first boot after an update, wait 10–15 minutes
If nothing changes:
Hold Power button for 10 seconds → shut down
Wait 30 seconds
Power ON again
📌 Temporary boot delays are common after updates.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disconnect External Devices
Power OFF the PC
Unplug all USB devices: [Pen drives External HDD/SSD Printer, webcam, dongles]
Keep only keyboard + mouse
Turn the PC ON
✔️ Faulty USB devices can stop Windows from loading.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Force Automatic Repair Mode
Turn ON the PC
When Windows logo appears → force shutdown
Repeat 2–3 times
You should see Preparing Automatic Repair
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Run Startup Repair
Advanced options → Troubleshoot
Advanced options → Startup Repair
Select your account and continue
✔️ Fixes damaged boot files automatically.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Uninstall Recent Windows Updates (MOST EFFECTIVE)
If Startup Repair fails:
Troubleshoot → Advanced options
Uninstall Updates
Choose:
Uninstall latest quality update
If still stuck → Uninstall latest feature update
📌 A bad update is a very common cause.
verification: PC should boot normally and reach login screen
tag: loading screen, boot, stuck, startup

user_error_text: I am getting a Windows license activation error
symptoms: Windows shows activation error, "Windows is not activated" message, error codes displayed
cause: Invalid product key, internet connectivity issues, Microsoft server problems, or edition mismatch
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check Activation Status (VERY IMPORTANT)
Go to Settings → System → Activation
Note the message shown:
"Windows is not activated"
Error code (example: 0xC004F074, 0x803F7001)
📌 The exact message helps identify the cause.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart PC & Check Internet
Restart your computer
Ensure you have a stable internet connection
Turn OFF VPN or proxy
✔️ Activation requires Microsoft servers.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Run Windows Activation Troubleshooter
Settings → System → Activation
Click Troubleshoot
Sign in with your Microsoft account (if asked)
✔️ Automatically fixes common activation problems.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Re-enter Product Key
Settings → System → Activation
Click Change product key
Enter your 25-character key
Click Activate
📌 Make sure the key matches your Windows edition (Home / Pro).
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Windows Edition Mismatch
Go to Settings → System → About
Check Edition (Home or Pro)

Try a different USB port (rear ports on desktops)

Test the drive on another computer

Plug in the external drive after Windows fully loads

Press Win + X → Disk Management
Look for your external drive (even if no letter)

No drive letter → Right-click → Change Drive Letter → Add
Offline → Right-click → Online

step_1:

Look at the USB flash drive / SD card
Some devices have a small LOCK switch
Move it to Unlock
Reinsert the drive and test again
📌 This is the most common and easiest cause.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Restart PC & Reconnect the Drive
Safely remove the drive
Restart the computer
Plug the drive back in after Windows fully loads
✔️ Clears temporary protection flags.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Remove Write Protection Using DiskPart (MOST EFFECTIVE)
⚠️ Follow carefully.
Press Win + X → Terminal (Admin) or Command Prompt (Admin)
Type commands one by one: diskpart & list disk
Identify your USB disk number (check size)
Then run:
select disk X [disk number]
attributes disk clear readonly
exit
✔️ This removes software-level write protection.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Check Registry Write-Protection Setting
Press Win + R → type regedit
Go to: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\StorageDevicePolicies
On the right: If WriteProtect exists → double-click → Set 0
Restart PC

step_5:
✅ Option 5: Format the Drive (⚠️ DATA LOSS)

Try a different cable

RAW
File system not recognized

user_error_text: I see a secure boot violation error during startup

step_1:
✅ Option 1: Restart and Enter BIOS / UEFI (VERY IMPORTANT)
Power ON the PC
Immediately press F2 / DEL / ESC / F10 (depends on brand)
Enter BIOS / UEFI Setup
📌 You must fix this from BIOS — Windows cannot load until it's resolved.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Check Boot Mode
In BIOS, find Boot Mode or Boot Configuration.
If Windows was installed in UEFI mode: ✔️ Boot Mode = UEFI
If Windows was installed in Legacy mode: ✔️ Boot Mode = Legacy / CSM
📌 Boot mode mismatch is the most common cause.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Disable Secure Boot (MOST EFFECTIVE)
In BIOS, go to Security or Boot
Find Secure Boot
Set it to Disabled
Save changes (F10 → Yes)
Restart PC
✔️ This fixes most Secure Boot Violation errors immediately.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Load Default Secure Boot Keys (If You Want Secure Boot ON)
In BIOS → Secure Boot
Set OS Type to: Windows UEFI Mode
Select Install Default Secure Boot Keys
Save and restart
📌 Required if keys were deleted or corrupted.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Boot Priority
Ensure Windows Boot Manager is:
At the top of boot order
Do NOT select: USB / Network / Old HDD entries first
✔️ Wrong boot device can trigger violation errors.

user_error_text: I see a CPU fan error message when starting the PC

Shut down the PC
Do NOT keep booting while this error appears

Open the PC case (desktop) or rear vents (laptop)
Power ON briefly and observe:

❌ Fan does NOT spin → fan failure
⚠️ Turn it OFF again immediately.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Check CPU Fan Cable Connection (MOST COMMON CAUSE)
Locate the CPU_FAN header on the motherboard

step_4:
✅ Option 4: Clean Dust From Fan & Heatsink
Use compressed air
Remove dust from: CPU fan blades & Heatsink fins
Make sure the fan can spin freely

step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check BIOS Fan Settings
Enter BIOS/UEFI (Del / F2)
Go to Hardware Monitor / Fan Control
Check: CPU fan speed (RPM)
Set: CPU Fan Speed = Auto / PWM
Low RPM Warning = Enabled (or reduce threshold if needed)

Unplug the charger
Remove the battery
Hold the Power button for 30 seconds
Reinsert the battery
Plug in the charger and power ON

Click the battery icon
Look for messages like: Plugged in, not charging

Check battery percentage behavior

Restart the laptop

step_5:
✅ Option 5: Update BIOS & Power Drivers
Visit the laptop manufacturer's website
Update: BIOS / UEFI / Chipset / Power Management drivers

Restore and restart

user_error_text: My RAM seems faulty and causes crashes
symptoms: System crashes, blue screens, random freezes, memory errors, file corruption
cause: Faulty RAM modules, loose connections, incompatible RAM, XMP/DOCP instability
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Stop Heavy Use Immediately (VERY IMPORTANT)
Shut down the PC if crashes are frequent
Avoid gaming, rendering, or heavy multitasking
📌 Continued use with bad RAM can corrupt files and Windows.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (FIRST TEST)
Press Win + R
Type mdsched.exe
Choose Restart now and check for problems
Let the test complete (PC will reboot)
Results:
❌ Errors found → RAM problem confirmed
✔️ No errors → still continue to Step 3 (not 100% reliable)
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Reseat the RAM Modules (MOST COMMON FIX)
Power OFF → unplug cable
Open the case
Remove RAM sticks
Clean contacts (air only, no liquid)
Reinsert firmly until clicks

symptoms: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT BSOD, system crash, memory error, blue screen with memory management stop code
cause: Faulty RAM, RAM incompatibility, corrupted system files, driver conflicts, overheating, memory paging errors
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Boot into Safe Mode (Critical Test)
hardware or drivers are at fault. If Windows boots:
Press Win + R
Type msconfig
Open Boot tab
Enable Safe boot → Minimal
Restart
If Windows won't boot:
Force power off during startup 3 times
Go to Automatic Repair → Advanced options
Troubleshoot → Startup Settings → Press 4
✔️ If BSOD does NOT happen in Safe Mode → RAM or driver issue confirmed.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Test RAM (MOST IMPORTANT FIX)
Press Win + R
Type: mdsched.exe
Choose Restart now and check for problems
Let the test finish
❌ If ANY error appears → RAM is bad
✔️ Remove one RAM stick and test again
✔️ Replace the faulty stick
⚠️ If you recently upgraded RAM, remove the new RAM immediately and retest.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Repair System Files
Corrupted memory-related system files can trigger this crash.
Open Command Prompt (Run as Administrator) and run: sfc /scannow
✔️ If it repairs files → Restart
❌ If it fails → Continue to Step 4
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Repair Windows Image (DISM)
Fixes deep Windows corruption affecting memory handling.
Run Command Prompt (Admin): DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
Restart after completion.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Disk & Paging File Errors
Memory paging depends on disk health.
Run: chkdsk C: /f /r
✔️ Type Y → Restart
⏳ Long scan = normal
verification: System should boot without MEMORY_MANAGEMENT BSOD errors
tag: memory management, bsod, blue screen, ram error, memory error

Repeat 3 times

Select: Advanced options → Troubleshoot
✔️ You are now in Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE)
step_2:

Go to: Advanced options → Startup Repair
Select your account
Enter password if asked
Let Windows attempt automatic repair
✔️ If it boots → problem solved
❌ If it fails → continue
step_3:

Go to: Advanced options → Startup Settings
Click Restart

❌ If it still blue screens → hardware or system corruption
step_4:

step_5:

user_error_text: I get a BSOD after logging into Windows
symptoms: BSOD after login, crash after user login, blue screen after entering password, system crash after login screen
cause: Startup drivers, startup programs, graphics driver, antivirus software, corrupted user profile, driver conflicts
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Boot into Safe Mode (MOST IMPORTANT)
Safe Mode prevents startup drivers & apps from loading.
On the login screen, hold Shift
Click Power → Restart
Go to: Troubleshoot → Advanced options → Startup Settings
Click Restart
Press 4 (Enable Safe Mode)
✔️ If Windows does NOT crash in Safe Mode, the problem is confirmed as:
Startup driver /Startup program / Antivirus /GPU driver
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disable All Startup Programs (COMMON FIX)
Many BSODs after login are caused by startup apps.
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc → Task Manager
Go to Startup tab
Disable ALL non-Microsoft entries
Restart PC normally
✔️ If BSOD stops → re-enable apps one by one to find the culprit.
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Update or Roll Back Graphics Driver (VERY COMMON CAUSE)
Graphics drivers load right after login.
Press Win + X → Device Manager
Expand Display adapters
Right-click GPU → choose: Roll Back Driver OR Uninstall device
Restart → Windows will load a safe driver
✔️ If fixed → install latest stable driver from manufacturer.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Uninstall Third-Party Antivirus / Security Tools
Security software hooks deeply into memory.
From Safe Mode: Go to Settings → Apps
Uninstall: Antivirus / Firewall tools / System cleaners / boosters
Restart
✔️ Windows Defender will protect you automatically.
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Repair System Files (ESSENTIAL)
Corrupted files can crash Windows after user login.
Open Command Prompt (Run as Administrator) and run: sfc /scannow
After that, run: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
Restart PC.
verification: Windows should boot and login without BSOD errors

step_2:

You must use Recovery because Windows can't boot.
Turn on PC
When Windows logo appears → hold Power button to turn OFF
Repeat 3 times
You'll see Automatic Repair
Go to: Advanced options → Troubleshoot
step_2:

Select your Windows account
Let Windows attempt repair
✔️ If Windows boots → fixed
❌ If not → continue
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Uninstall Recent Windows Update (VERY COMMON FIX)
This error often appears right after an update.
Go to: Advanced options → Uninstall Updates
First select: Uninstall latest quality update
If still broken: Uninstall latest feature update
Restart PC
✔️ This fixes many systems instantly.
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Check BIOS / UEFI Storage Mode (CRITICAL)
A wrong disk mode will break boot access.
Restart PC → Enter BIOS / UEFI (Del / F2 / F10 / Esc)

error_name: Computer Does Not Boot Into Windows

cause: Power issues, BIOS settings, corrupted boot files, disk errors, hardware failure, system file corruption
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Power Reset (Very Important & Easy)
For desktop :
Turn off the PC & Unplug the power cable
Hold the Power button for 15 seconds & Plug back in and turn on
For laptop :
Shut down & Remove charger (and battery if removable)
Hold Power button for 15 seconds & Reconnect and start
✔️ If it boots → problem solved
❌ If not → continue
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Check BIOS / UEFI Boot Settings
Turn on PC
Immediately press DEL / F2 / F10 / F12 / ESC (depends on motherboard)
Enter BIOS / UEFI
Check: Boot Mode → UEFI (for Windows 10/11)
Windows Boot Manager is first
Choose Load Optimized Defaults
Save & Exit (F10)
✔️ Reboot and test
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Try Automatic Startup Repair
Power on → interrupt boot 3 times (hold power during loading)
You'll see Preparing Automatic Repair
Go to: Advanced options → Troubleshoot → Startup Repair
Select your Windows account
✔️ Let Windows repair itself
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Boot into Safe Mode
Safe Mode loads minimal drivers.
Advanced options
Troubleshoot → Advanced options
Startup Settings → Restart
Press 4 or F4 (Safe Mode)
If Safe Mode works:
Uninstall recent drivers
Uninstall recent Windows updates
Remove recently installed software
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Disk & System Files (Advanced but Effective)
Advanced options → Command Prompt
Run these commands one by one:
chkdsk c: /f /r
sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows

verification: Windows should boot normally into the desktop

step_5:

user_error_text: Startup repair keeps running and never finishes

cause: Corrupted system files, disk errors, bad sectors, Windows update corruption, boot configuration issues
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Break the Startup Repair Loop
Power ON the PC
When Startup Repair starts → hold Power button to force shutdown
Repeat 2–3 times
You should see Advanced options
✔️ If you reach Choose an option, continue
❌ If not → tell me (possible hardware failure)
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disable Automatic Startup Repair (MOST EFFECTIVE)
Advanced options → Troubleshoot
Advanced options → Command Prompt
Type exactly and press Enter: bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No
Close Command Prompt
Restart PC
✔️ This stops Windows from looping into Startup Repair
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Repair Disk Errors (VERY IMPORTANT)
Still in Command Prompt, run: chkdsk c: /f /r
⏳ May take 30–90 minutes
⚠️ Do NOT interrupt
✔️ Fixes bad sectors that cause endless repair
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Repair Windows System Files
After chkdsk completes:
sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows
✔️ Repairs corrupted Windows files
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Uninstall the Broken Windows Update
Advanced options
Uninstall Updates
First choose Uninstall latest quality update
If still stuck → Uninstall feature update
✔️ Updates are the #1 cause of this loop
verification: PC should boot normally without getting stuck in startup repair
tag: startup repair never finishes, repair stuck, endless repair loop, repair hangs

user_error_text: Windows shows boot error code 0x74
symptoms: Boot error 0x74, error code 0x74 at startup, Windows boot failure 0x74, system cannot boot 0x74
cause: File system corruption, disk errors, corrupted boot files, registry corruption, system file damage
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Enter Windows Recovery (WinRE)
Power ON the PC
When Windows logo appears → hold Power button to force OFF
Repeat 3 times
You should see Preparing Automatic Repair
Select Advanced options
✔️ If you reach Choose an option, continue
❌ If not → possible hardware issue
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Run Startup Repair (Quick Check)
Advanced options
Troubleshoot
Startup Repair
Select your account
✔️ If Windows boots → done
❌ If repair fails → continue
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Repair Disk Errors (VERY IMPORTANT)
Advanced options → Command Prompt
Run: chkdsk c: /f /r
⏳ May take 30–90 minutes
✔️ Fixes file system corruption causing 0x74
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Repair Windows System Files
After chkdsk finishes, run: sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows
✔️ Repairs corrupted Windows files and registry links
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Rebuild Boot Configuration (MOST EFFECTIVE)
Still in Command Prompt, run one by one:
bootrec /fixmbr
bootrec /fixboot
bootrec /scanos
bootrec /rebuildbcd
If asked to add installation → type Y and press Enter
✔️ Restores broken boot configuration
⚠️ If "Access is denied" appears
Run this, then retry Option 5: bootsect /nt60 sys OR bootsect /nt60 all
verification: Windows should boot without error code 0x74
tag: boot error 0x74, error code 0x74, windows boot failure 0x74, system cannot boot

user_error_text: My system is stuck on the loading screen
symptoms: PC stuck on loading screen, Windows loading never completes, system hangs on startup, loading screen freeze
cause: USB device conflicts, driver issues, corrupted system files, Windows update problems, hardware failure
step_1:

Desktop :
Power OFF & Unplug power cable
Hold Power button 15 seconds & Plug in and start
Laptop :
Shut down & Unplug charger (remove battery if possible)
Hold Power button 20 seconds & Reconnect and start
✔️ If it boots → done
❌ Still stuck → continue
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Disconnect External Devices
Power OFF
Remove all USB devices (printers, drives, hubs)
Leave only keyboard & mouse
Power ON
✔️ Faulty USB devices can hang startup
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Enter Windows Recovery (WinRE)
Power ON
When Windows logo appears → hold Power to force OFF
Repeat 3 times
You should see Preparing Automatic Repair
Select Advanced options
✔️ If you reach Choose an option, continue
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Use Startup Repair
Troubleshoot
Startup Repair
Select your Windows account
✔️ If Windows loads → solved
❌ If it fails → continue
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Boot into Safe Mode (Driver Check)
Advanced options → Startup Settings
Click Restart
Press 4 or F4 (Safe Mode)
If Safe Mode works:
Uninstall recent drivers (especially GPU)
Uninstall recent Windows updates
Remove third-party antivirus
Restart normally
✔️ Confirms a software/driver issue
verification: System should boot past the loading screen into Windows
tag: stuck on loading screen, loading never completes, startup freeze, loading screen hang

Turn OFF your router and modem
Unplug power cables
Wait 30–60 seconds
Plug them back in

step_2:

Run the test

step_4:
✅ Option 4: Disconnect Other Devices
Turn off Wi-Fi on unused phones, TVs, tablets
Pause downloads / streaming on other devices
✔️ Too many devices can slow the network
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Restart Your Computer
Click Start → Restart
Do NOT shut down — choose Restart
✔️ Clears network cache & stuck processes
verification: Internet speed should return to normal levels

error_name: Internet Speed Dropped After Router Restart
user_error_text: Internet speed dropped after router restart
symptoms: Slow internet after router restart, speed decreased after reboot, network slower after restart
cause: Router configuration reset, wrong Wi-Fi band, channel interference, QoS settings, ISP sync issues
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Power-Cycle Router & Modem (MOST IMPORTANT)
Turn OFF router and modem
Unplug power cables
Wait 60 seconds
Plug modem first, wait till stable
Plug router, wait 2–3 minutes
✔️ Restores proper sync with ISP
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Run a Speed Test (Baseline)
Go to speedtest.net or fast.com
Note Download / Upload / Ping
✔️ Compare with your plan speed
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Check Wi-Fi Band (Common After Restart)
Connect to 5 GHz (faster, shorter range)
Use 2.4 GHz if far from router
✔️ Routers often switch bands after reboot
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Change Wi-Fi Channel (Reduces Interference)
Open router admin page (usually 192.168.1.1)
Wireless settings → Channel
Set Auto or try: 2.4 GHz: 1 / 6 / 11 & 5 GHz: 36 / 40 / 44 / 48
Save & reboot router
✔️ Fixes congestion from nearby networks
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Disable Bandwidth-Hungry Features
In router settings, turn OFF temporarily:
QoS (Quality of Service)
Traffic monitoring
Parental controls

step_2:

step_3:

Turn OFF Kill Switch
Turn OFF Block internet if VPN disconnects
✔️ Kill Switch can block all traffic
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Turn OFF Split Tunneling (Test)
VPN app → Split Tunneling
Disable it completely
Reconnect VPN
✔️ Misconfigured split tunneling breaks routing
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Windows Proxy Settings
Win + I → Network & Internet → Proxy
Turn OFF: Use a proxy server
✔️ VPN + proxy conflict = no internet
verification: Internet should work with VPN connected

step_2:

Restart PC
Re-check network settings

Disable suspicious or repeated reset tasks

step_5:
✅ Option 5: Fix Corrupt Network Driver (VERY EFFECTIVE)
Win + X → Device Manager
Expand Network adapters

Restart PC

Turn it ON
Restart your PC

Expand Network adapters
Right-click Wi-Fi adapter → Properties
Open Power Management tab

step_3:

Control Panel → Power Options

Try Update driver first

Manage known networks

error_name: Disk Structure Is Corrupted and Unreadable
user_error_text: Disk structure is corrupted and unreadable
symptoms: Disk structure corrupted, unreadable disk, cannot access drive, disk corruption error
cause: File system corruption, bad sectors, sudden power loss, disk failure, corrupted partition table
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Restart Your PC (Quick Fix)
Sometimes the error is temporary.
✔️ Restart Windows normally
✔️ Try opening the drive again
👉 If still not accessible, continue.
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Run CHKDSK (MOST IMPORTANT)
This repairs file system corruption and bad sectors.
Press Win + X
Click Command Prompt (Admin) or Windows Terminal (Admin)
Type : chkdsk X: /f /r
Press Enter
If asked to schedule → type Y → Restart PC
✔️ /f fixes errors
✔️ /r recovers bad sectors

⏳ May take time — do not interrupt
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Check Drive in Disk Management
Confirms if Windows detects the disk correctly.
Press Win + R
Type: diskmgmt.msc
Press Enter
✔️ If drive shows RAW → file system is corrupted
✔️ If No Drive Letter → right-click → Change Drive Letter → Add

❌ If disk shows Unallocated → do NOT format yet
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Run System File Checker (Internal Drives)
If this affects C: drive or system disk.
Open Command Prompt (Admin)
Run: sfc /scannow
✔️ Repairs damaged Windows system files
✔️ Restart after completion
step_5:
✅ Option 5: Check Disk Health (SMART Status)
Detects physical disk failure.
Open Command Prompt
Run: wmic diskdrive get status
✔️ OK → disk is healthy
❌ Pred Fail / Bad → disk is dying (backup immediately)
verification: Disk should be accessible and readable
tag: disk structure corrupted, unreadable disk, disk corruption, cannot access drive

user_error_text: Partition is missing or deleted
symptoms: Partition missing, deleted partition, unallocated space, partition not found, drive disappeared
cause: Accidental deletion, partition table corruption, disk errors, malware, system crash, user error
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Check Disk Management
Confirm whether the partition is actually missing.
Press Win + R
Type: diskmgmt.msc
Press Enter
🔍 Look for:
Unallocated space → partition deleted
RAW partition → file system damaged
Disk Offline → right-click → Online
No drive letter → Change Drive Letter → Add
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Rescan Disks
Sometimes Windows just didn't refresh.
In Disk Management
Click Action → Rescan Disks
✔️ If partition reappears → assign a drive letter
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Use DiskPart (Advanced Check)
Confirms if partition table exists.
Open Command Prompt (Admin)
Run: diskpart
list disk 
select disk 0 
list volume
🔍 If volume is missing → partition table is damaged or deleted
❌ Do NOT use clean
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Recover the Lost Partition (BEST OPTION)
Use partition recovery (read-only scan).
✔️ Scan entire disk
✔️ Restore partition table
✔️ Save recovered partition
⚠️ Choose "Recover Partition", not file-only recovery
step_5:
✅ Option 5: If Partition Shows RAW
Try repairing the file system first.
chkdsk X: /f
✔️ Works only if file system is damaged but partition exists
verification: Partition should be visible and accessible
tag: partition missing, deleted partition, unallocated space, partition not found

user_error_text: CHKDSK shows errors repeatedly
symptoms: CHKDSK errors keep appearing, repeated disk errors, bad clusters increasing, file system errors recurring
cause: Physical disk failure, bad sectors spreading, controller failure, disk wear, manufacturing defects
step_1:
✅ Option 1: Confirm the Pattern
Run CHKDSK once more to verify.
RUN : chkdsk C: /f /r
🔍 If you see the same messages again like:
"Windows replaced bad clusters"
"Correcting errors in the master file table (MFT)"
"File record segment is unreadable"
➡️ This confirms physical disk problems
step_2:
✅ Option 2: Check SMART Disk Health
This tells if the disk is failing.
Open Command Prompt
Run: wmic diskdrive get status
✔️ OK → early-stage failure
❌ Pred Fail / Bad → disk is dying
step_3:
✅ Option 3: Identify Disk Type (HDD vs SSD)
This affects the decision.
✔️ HDD → bad sectors spread over time
✔️ SSD → repeated errors mean controller / NAND failure
⚠️ SSDs should be replaced immediately if errors repeat
step_4:
✅ Option 4: Run System File Repair (System Drive Only)
RUN : sfc /scannow
